text:
The Rangers arrive in Seattle at 2-3-0 over their last five, outscored 20-14, though they've won two straight, including 3-2 over Philadelphia on Wednesday. They're without defenseman Sean Durzi and goalie Igor Shesterkin, so Adam Fox is playing 24:17 a night. The Kraken, 3-2-0 in their last five, won 2-1 over Calgary in overtime on Matty Beniers' goal. They're missing Jared McCann, whose minutes have gone to Jordan Eberle beside Beniers. Two Rangers, Tye Kartye and Eeli Tolvanen, return to their old building for the first time.

Our numbers favor New York in how the play unfolds. At five on five, the Rangers have taken 52% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) and Seattle 45%. Our model has NYR at 3.21 goals tonight and SEA at 2.85. Special teams are close: the NYR power play is worth 0.66 expected goals a game and SEA's 0.58. In net, projected starter Dylan Garand sits at +2.2 goals saved above expected (how many goals better than the shots he faced deserved), while Philipp Grubauer is at -1.5 and has struggled lately.

Among players to watch, Pavel Dorofeyev is our under-the-radar pick. He skates on the third line but has put up 4.8 expected goals in his last 10 games, and we give him a 31% chance to score. Alexis Lafrenière, the first overall pick in 2020, is at 30%. For Seattle, Berkly Catton carries a seven-game point streak into the game.
